params.place: on the map: the Gulf, the strait between Iran and Oman

moments.what: tankers already file through the narrow strait, the name HORMUZ writing on
the strait's two shores trace in light, Iran above and Oman below
a red barrier slams down across the water
a DAY ONE counter sign plants on the shore
the camera pulls back over the whole Gulf
the tankers bunch up behind the barrier
a question mark bounces over the Gulf

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The Strait of Hormuz shuts for a week. Which country runs out first?

params.place: on the map: the strait seen close, the shipping lane

moments.what: the camera glides along the shipping lane
a sun crosses the sky sign
barrels stack up on the tankers' decks
a stream of tankers runs through the lane, the counter on a buoy counting up
the lane narrows between the two shores
the two-way lane draws on the water
Iran's mountains rise along the north shore
Oman's tip glows on the south shore
the buoy sign bobs up
the counter on the buoy lands

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Every day, about 20.9M barrels of oil sail through this one gap, a lane of sea between Iran's mountains and the tip of Oman.

params.place: on the map: the Gulf from the strait to Kuwait

moments.what: the counter sign flips to DAY ONE
tankers line up along the Gulf
they halt with a jolt
Kuwait traces and fills with its flag
Qatar traces and fills with its flag
Bahrain traces and fills with its flag
the barrier at the strait glows red
the stuck tankers turn round
they bump into the shore and the barrier

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Day one: the tankers stop. Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain are stuck behind the gate, and their ships have nowhere else to go.

params.place: on the map: the Gulf's inner shore

moments.what: the camera sweeps along the Gulf's inner shore
the four countries' coastlines glow
a bright line runs along their whole coast
the line stays inside the Gulf, ending short of the strait
the Gulf's water darkens like a closed room
the barrier at the strait glows like a shut door

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Look at the map: every bit of their coast lies inside the Gulf, like a room with only one door.

params.place: on the map: Saudi Arabia from the Gulf to the Red Sea

moments.what: the counter sign flips to DAY TWO
Saudi Arabia traces
it fills with its flag
an arrow curls round the strait
a pipe starts drawing from the Gulf coast
it runs west
across the sand, dunes on either side
it reaches the Red Sea coast
a tanker loads at the Red Sea port

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Day two: Saudi Arabia has a way round, a pipeline west across the desert to the Red Sea.

params.place: on the map: the Emirates and the coast past the strait

moments.what: the counter sign flips to DAY THREE
the Emirates trace and fill with their flag
a pipe draws east across the Emirates
a pin drops on Fujairah
cranes pop up at the port
the camera shows the port on the far side of the barrier
a tanker slips away from the port

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Day three: the Emirates pipe oil to Fujairah, a port just outside the strait.

params.place: on the map: the whole Gulf, both pipes and the blocked strait

moments.what: both pipelines glow
oil drips out of their ends
a thin trickle beside a fat stream of tankers
the trickle shrinks
the stuck tankers behind the barrier bob
oil barrels pile up on the docks

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But those two pipes carry only a small part of what the tankers did, and the rest has nowhere to go.

params.place: on the map: Asia, the routes east from Hormuz

moments.what: the counter sign flips to DAY FOUR
the tankers at Hormuz stay put, the dashed routes east stay empty
China traces and fills with its flag
India traces and fills with its flag
Japan traces and fills with its flag
South Korea traces
it fills with its flag
a fat arrow from Hormuz points east
the arrow sweeps across the Indian Ocean
the empty routes to Asia's ports blink

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Day four: no new tankers leave for China, India, Japan or South Korea, and most of the oil through Hormuz sails east to Asia.

params.place: on the map: Iran's Gulf coast and Kharg Island

moments.what: a question mark spins over Iran
Iran traces and fills with its flag
a tanker sets off from Kharg Island
a pin drops on Kharg, deep inside the Gulf
the tanker's route runs to the barrier and stops
Iran's own tanker bobs stuck behind its own barrier
KHARG ISLAND writes on beside the pin

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And the strangest part? Iran ships most of its own oil from inside the Gulf too, from an island called Kharg.

params.place: on the map: the Gulf and the whole world beyond the strait

moments.what: the counter sign flips to DAY FIVE
Kuwait lights up
Qatar lights up
Bahrain lights up
oil tanks on their coasts fill to the brim
the camera pushes toward the strait
a road of light runs from their coasts to the barrier and stops
a big sign over the strait shows the share
the camera pulls back to the world, lines spreading from the strait
the share sign pulses
the world's coastlines glow where the lines reach

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So who runs out first? Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain run out of ways to sell their oil: this gap is their only road out, and it carries about 20% of all the oil the world uses.

params.place: on the map: Asia from Hormuz to Malacca, then back to Hormuz

moments.what: a pin pulses at Hormuz
the camera swings east and a pin drops at the Strait of Malacca
both straits glow
a barrier hovers over Malacca
a comment bubble pops
the shores' glow fades back to the first frame, tankers filing through
the bubble wobbles
the camera starts diving back west to Hormuz
the strait's shores come into view as in the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Hormuz or Malacca: which strait should we shut next? Tell me below, while the Strait of Hormuz shuts for a week.
